Only `https` servers on public hosts and `npx` or `uvx` servers are accepted; a refused server prints `Not added: REASON` and exits with status 1. `--allow-literal` asks you to confirm and then copies the real token to the machines — into the worker's own config file — instead of using an Instabox secret. All of this is described in [MCP servers for subagents](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/mcp.html).

### cloudy-cloud mcp-server

```
cloudy-cloud mcp-server
```

Runs the Cloudy Cloud MCP server on stdio, for MCP clients other than the built-in hosts. It prints nothing itself and runs before the setup check, so an empty config still answers `tools/list`. The server reads its keys from `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/env` itself. Claude Code, Codex, opencode and pi sessions get the same tools through their own `cloudy-cloud` host command.

## Tools the session uses (MCP)

`cloudy-cloud` adds an MCP server named `cloud` to the session. Claude sees its tools as `mcp__cloud__cloud_agent` and so on. The session is configured to allow these six tools without asking and to deny the built-in `Agent` and `Workflow` tools. You normally ask for subagents in plain language and Claude calls the tools. This section is for when you want to know exactly what each tool takes.

In a terminal Claude Code session that supports MCP tasks, `cloud_agent` and `cloud_agent_message` run as background tasks. Their progress shows in `/tasks` and the result arrives on its own with the agent id, so Claude does not need `cloud_agent_wait`. In other clients these two tools return an agent id at once and Claude calls `cloud_agent_wait`. The server also answers the task methods `tasks/get` and `tasks/cancel`.

### cloud_agent

Starts a subagent in a remote sandbox on the committed and tracked files of the current repository. It does not include untracked files. The repository needs a `github.com` origin. The call returns at once while the sandbox starts and the task runs. The agent pushes its work to the origin branch `cloudy-cloud/<id>`. Nothing is copied into your local repository. The agent stays open for follow-ups until it is stopped or has been idle for 60 minutes.

Each turn is limited to 29 minutes by default. `CLOUDY_CLOUD_TURN_MINUTES` changes the limit (see Settings), and the prompt tells the agent when its turn ends. If a turn fails or hits the limit after the agent has started, the agent stays open with its session: call `cloud_agent_message` to continue it. A worker that commits nothing pushes no branch; the result says `No changes, no branch pushed.` and autofix does not start.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `prompt` | string | yes | none | The full task for the subagent. |
| `description` | string | yes | none | A short label for the task. |
| `model` | string | no | the Claude default | A Claude model name, such as `haiku`. For a non-Claude model, use `profile` instead. It is needed with a profile only for `openrouter`, `codex-openrouter` and `opencode-openrouter`, which have no built-in model. It may contain only letters, digits and `. _ : -`. When `profile` is also set, `/` is allowed too. |
| `profile` | string | no | Claude | Runs the worker on another agent or model. Built in: `glm`, `deepseek`, `particle` and `openrouter` (Claude Code on another model); `pi-glm`, `pi-deepseek` and `pi-particle` (pi); `omp-glm`, `omp-deepseek` and `omp-particle` (oh-my-pi); `codex`, `codex-chatgpt` and `codex-openrouter` (Codex); `opencode-glm`, `opencode-deepseek`, `opencode-particle` and `opencode-openrouter` (opencode). You can add names in `profiles.json`, where each entry's `harness` (`claude`, `pi`, `omp`, `codex` or `opencode`) says which agent runs the worker. An unknown name, or a profile whose key is missing, makes the call fail at once. See [Models and keys](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/models.html). |
| `role` | string, `worker` or `coordinator` | no | `worker` | A worker does the task. A coordinator also gets cloudy-cloud installed and can start its own cloud agents, limited by `CLOUDY_CLOUD_MAX_DEPTH` (default 3). A coordinator always runs Claude Code, so it cannot use a pi, omp, Codex or opencode profile. |
| `machine` | string | no | `linux` | The kind of machine: `linux`, `android`, `omarchy`, `gpu`, `gpu:TYPE`, `gpu:TYPE:COUNT` (COUNT 1 to 4 for any GPU type), `macos` or `macos:MODEL`. `gpu` and `macos` cost much more (GPU: from $0.765 per GPU-hour; Mac: $0.45 to $1.25 per hour with a 24-hour minimum) and are refused until `CLOUDY_CLOUD_ALLOW_MACHINE_KINDS` in `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/env` names them (for example `gpu,macos`). Only on Instabox. |
| `size` | string | no | `4x8` | Machine size as VCPUSxGIB, for example `2x4`, `4x8` or `8x16`. Your Instabox plan decides which sizes are allowed; a size no plan lists is refused. |
| `autofix` | boolean | no | `false` | After the worker pushes, the server opens a pull request for its branch and keeps the worker fixing failed checks, review comments and merge conflicts, for at most `CLOUDY_CLOUD_AUTOFIX_ROUNDS` rounds, before the task ends. The result says whether the pull request is clean. Not for coordinators. |
| `base` | string | no | the local `HEAD` | A branch name or a commit hash of 7 to 40 hex characters. The worker starts from it instead of your local `HEAD`; the server fetches it from origin if needed. Uncommitted edits are ignored when `base` is set. |
| `fallback` | array of strings | no | the profile's `fallback` in `profiles.json`, else none | Profile names to try, in order, when the chosen profile has no key or the provider refuses the one-token check before the machine starts. It overrides the profile's own `fallback`. The result says which profile ran. |
| `preflight` | boolean | no | `true` | Set `false` to skip the one-token provider check that runs before the machine is created. |
| `subagent_type` | string | no | none | The name of an agent to run, passed to Claude Code as `--agent` (Claude Code workers only). It may contain only letters, digits and `. _ : -`. |
| `issue` | string | no | none | A GitHub issue in this repo's origin: a number like `"12"`, or a URL like `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n>`. The title and body are fetched on your computer with `gh` and quoted into the prompt as untrusted text. The branch is `cloudy-cloud/issue-<n>-<id>`, and an autofix pull request body says `Fixes #<n>`, so merging it closes the issue. Workers only; needs `gh` signed in. |
| `preview_port` | integer | no | none | A port from 1 to 65535 (a digit string also works) where the worker's app is already running on its machine. After a turn that pushed, a share link is published, the same as `cloudy-cloud open <id> <port> --share`, and the result shows `Preview: <url>`. The link is never posted to a pull request. Anyone with the link can open the app until the machine is deleted. Needs a provider that supports published links (Instabox); if publishing fails, the turn still succeeds and the result gives the manual command. |

When `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/mcp.json` holds at least one valid server, a Claude Code subagent (not a pi, omp, Codex or opencode worker) starts with `--mcp-config` for that file and `--strict-mcp-config`, so a repo's own `.mcp.json` is not loaded on the machine. pi, omp, Codex and opencode workers get the same servers in their own config files. The reply ends with an `MCP servers:` line. See [MCP servers for subagents](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/mcp.html).

The call is refused if the session has already started `CLOUDY_CLOUD_MAX_AGENTS_PER_SESSION` agents (default 200), or if the folder is not a git repository with at least one commit and a `github.com` origin.

### cloud_agent_message

Sends a follow-up message to an open agent that is idle, and continues the same conversation. It returns at once. As an MCP task the reply arrives on its own. Otherwise Claude calls `cloud_agent_wait`. It is rejected if the agent is busy or gone.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agent_id` | string | yes | none | The id returned by `cloud_agent`. |
| `message` | string | yes | none | The follow-up text. |

### cloud_agent_wait

Waits until every listed agent finishes its current turn, or until the timeout passes. For each agent it returns the status (`starting`, `running`, `idle`, `failed` or `stopped`) and its latest result. Each result is returned once. Later calls mark it as already reported. The tool is read-only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agent_ids` | array of strings | yes | none | The agent ids to wait for. |
| `timeout_seconds` | number | no | 600 | How long to wait. Values above 1500 are limited to 1500. |

### cloud_agent_result

Returns an agent's latest result again, as often as asked, even after `cloud_agent_wait` or a task notification delivered it. If the agent has no result yet it says `no result yet, status running`. If the agent is not open it returns an error with a next step. The tool is read-only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agent_id` | string | yes | The agent id. |

### cloud_agent_list

Lists every agent with its id, description, status, idle minutes and progress (tool uses, tokens, elapsed time and current step). The tool is read-only. With `all: true` it instead lists every machine on the provider labelled `purpose=cloudy-cloud` (other sessions and coordinators included), grouped by its `parent` label. Each worker machine carries the labels `role`, `profile` (`claude` for the default), `parent`, `agent` and a short redacted `description`.

### cloud_agent_stop

Stops agents and deletes their sandboxes. It is safe to repeat, and safe to call with ids that do not exist. Stop agents when they are finished, because they stay open until stopped or idle for 60 minutes.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agent_ids` | array of strings | yes | none | The agent ids to stop. |

### Limits that apply to the tools

- An agent that is idle for 60 minutes is stopped. Every agent is stopped when the session ends.
- A single task is stopped after 29 minutes.
- Machines start at most `CLOUDY_CLOUD_STARTS_PER_MIN` times a minute. Agents waiting for a machine show the status `queued`.
- Instabox deletes every machine the tool creates after `CLOUDY_CLOUD_WORKER_HOURS` hours, even if `cloudy-cloud` has died.

## Kinds of machines

The `machine` argument of cloud_agent picks the machine. Prices are Instabox's ([pricing](https://instabox.sh/docs/account/pricing.md)). Live facts are from one run on 2026-11-15.

| machine | What it is | Price | Consent | Display |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `linux` | The standard machine (default). | Your plan | no | yes |
| `android` | Android emulator with `adb`. Its desktop starts in about 1 second. | Not checked | no | yes |
| `gpu` | NVIDIA GPU (one L4 by default). The first desktop start takes about 2 minutes. | $0.765 per GPU-hour (NVIDIA L4) | yes | yes |
| `omarchy` | Omarchy Linux with a Hyprland desktop. `display` and `--screenshot` are refused; `shell` works. | Not checked | no | no |
| `macos` | A Mac, for Xcode builds. Experimental, not yet run live. | $0.45 to $1.25 per hour, 24-hour minimum lease | yes | not verified |

See cloudy-cloud shell and cloudy-cloud display to look at a machine.

## Environment variables and files

Environment variables win over values in the config file. An empty value counts as unset.

### Keys

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `INSTABOX_API_KEY` | none | Your Instabox API key. Read from the environment or the config file. |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` | none | The long-lived token from `claude setup-token`. Cloud agents use it to sign in to Claude. |
| `GH_TOKEN` | none | Your GitHub token. On a self-hosted machine it is read from the config file and placed in each worker container if you allowed that. See [Run on your own machine](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/self-hosted.html#github-token). |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | none | An Anthropic API key, used by cloud agents when there is no Claude token. It is billed separately. |
| `PARTICLE_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, and any other name ending in `_API_KEY` | none | Provider keys for model profiles. A profile's `keyName` must name one of these. A worker that uses a profile receives that profile's key. |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | none | Your OpenAI API key, for the `codex` profile. Setup asks for it when you choose codex. See [The codex profiles](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/models.html#codex-profiles). |

> Note: The launcher only checks the config file for the Claude token, not the environment, so save it there with `cloudy-cloud setup`. The Instabox key can come from either place.

### Settings

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_CONFIG` | `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/env` | Path of the config file. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_ALLOW_MACHINE_KINDS` | none | Comma-separated machine kinds you allow although they cost much more: `gpu`, `macos`. Without it, `cloud_agent` refuses those kinds and starts nothing. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_PROVIDER` | `instabox` | Sandbox provider: `instabox`, `self-hosted` or `microsandbox`. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_MSB_BIN` | `~/.local/bin/msb`, then `msb` on PATH | Microsandbox: path of the `msb` program. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_MSB_SLOTS` | 2 | Microsandbox: how many microVMs run at once. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_EGRESS_ALLOW` | unset | Hosts a worker machine may connect to, separated by commas or spaces; `*.example.com` covers the domain and its subdomains. The worker can also always reach `github.com`, `api.github.com`, its model host and every configured `https` MCP server host, plus DNS. `off` (or `none`) sets no policy on purpose. Only the `microsandbox` provider enforces the list; on another provider `cloud_agent` refuses to start while it is set, and a set-but-empty value is an error. Workers only, and only Claude Code workers that reach their model host directly. See [Troubleshooting](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/troubleshooting.html). |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` | unset | Set to `1` to turn off the update notice. The check for a newer version runs once a day; a notice already in the cache can print on every launch. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_SELF_HOSTED_COORDINATORS` | unset | Self-hosted, written by setup: `yes` means coordinators on your machine may start containers through Docker. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_SELF_HOSTED_LOCAL` | unset | Self-hosted, set on a coordinator container: workers start as sibling containers on the same machine instead of over SSH. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_SELF_HOSTED_CONSENT_HOST` | unset | Self-hosted, written by setup: the machine the GitHub-token and Docker consents apply to. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_DOCKER_SOCKET` | `/var/run/docker.sock` | Self-hosted local mode: path of the Docker socket on the machine. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_CLAUDE_JSON` | `~/.claude.json` | The Claude Code settings file `cloudy-cloud mcp add` reads servers from. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_STREAMS` | `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/streams` | Folder of the redacted per-agent stream copies the dashboard reads. Pruning (`dashboard --prune`, and once at each agent's first turn) deletes any file in it by age and size, not only stream files. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_STREAM_THINKING` | unset | The stored streams keep the redacted raw lines either way; set to `1` where the dashboard runs to show thinking text instead of only its length. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_OPENCODE_BIN` | `opencode` | Program `cloudy-cloud opencode` runs. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_CODEX_AUTH` | `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/codex-auth.json` | Path of the ChatGPT login file the `codex-chatgpt` profile copies to a machine. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_DOCTOR_SLOW_MS` | 5000 | Milliseconds before the SSH probe in `doctor` and self-hosted setup is reported as slow. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_INSTABOX_API_KEY` | unset | Set on a coordinator machine: a placeholder for the Instabox key, which the launcher reads when `INSTABOX_API_KEY` is not set. You do not set it. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_SSH_HOST` | none | Self-hosted: the SSH address of your machine, `user@host`. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_SSH_KEY` | none | Self-hosted: path to the SSH key. Optional. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_SSH_PORT` | the SSH default | Self-hosted: the SSH port, when it is not the default. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_CONTAINER_RUNTIME` | `docker` | Self-hosted: `docker` or `podman`. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_CONTAINER_BIN` | none | Self-hosted: absolute path of the `docker` or `podman` program on the machine. Setup finds and saves it. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_SELF_HOSTED_SLOTS` | 2 if unset; setup suggests half the CPUs or one per 4 GB of memory, whichever is lower | Self-hosted: how many subagents run at once. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_SELF_HOSTED_CPUS` | 2 if unset | Self-hosted: CPU limit per container. Setup saves a value. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_SELF_HOSTED_MEMORY` | 4g if unset | Self-hosted: memory limit per container. Setup saves a value. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_SELF_HOSTED_TOKEN_ON_BOX` | unset | Self-hosted: `yes` means you allowed the GitHub token inside worker containers on your machine. Without it, workers do not start. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_PROFILES` | `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/profiles.json` | Path of the file that adds or overrides model profiles. Each entry can set `harness` to choose the agent (`claude`, `pi`, `omp`, `codex` or `opencode`), `fallback` (profile names to try in order) and `maxConcurrent` (a positive whole number). |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_MCP` | `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/mcp.json` | Path of the file that lists the MCP servers cloud subagents get. If the file is missing, no servers are sent. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_EVENTS` | `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/events.jsonl` | Path of the event log that the dashboard reads. Set it in the environment before you start `cloudy-cloud` and the dashboard. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_WORKER_HOURS` | 6 | Hours until the server deletes a worker or nested coordinator machine. At most 24. A value that is not a positive number uses 6. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_STARTS_PER_MIN` | 25 | The most machine starts per minute. Extra agents wait in the queue. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_MAX_INSTABOX_CALLS` | 24 | The most Instabox command and file requests that run at once. Instabox's own limit is 32. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_TURN_MINUTES` | 29 | The most minutes one agent turn may run. A whole number from 5 to the provider's machine lifetime in minutes minus 30; any other value is refused with the allowed range. The server sets `CLOUDY_CLOUD_TURN_DEADLINE` (the turn's end time) inside the worker command. You do not set it. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_PROVIDER_RETRIES` | 3 | How many times a pi, omp, Codex or opencode turn is retried after a transient provider error (model not found, 429, 5xx or a connection error). Errors such as 400, 401 and 403 are not retried. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_PROFILE_MAX` | no cap | The default most agents one profile may run at once. A profile's `maxConcurrent` in `profiles.json` overrides it. Agents over the cap wait in the queue and say why in `cloud_agent_list`. The count covers this server's own agents only. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_AUTOFIX_ROUNDS` | 3 | The most fix rounds `autofix` runs on a pull request (0 to 10). |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_MAX_DEPTH` | 3 | How many levels of coordinators can exist below your session. Starting a coordinator past this is refused. Workers do not add depth. Passed down to child coordinators. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_MAX_AGENTS_PER_SESSION` | 200 | How many agents one cloudy-cloud session may start. Passed down to child coordinators. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_PROXY_SECRETS` | empty | Comma-separated names of Instabox secrets that hold your Claude token and provider keys, for example `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN,PARTICLE_API_KEY,OPENROUTER_API_KEY`. A worker that needs a listed key gets the secret by name, so no key value reaches its environment. A key not listed is still copied to the machine, and the agent reply says so. Has no effect on providers without proxy secrets. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_APT_PACKAGES` | empty | Space-separated Debian package names (for example `ffmpeg postgresql-client`) that each worker installs with `sudo -n apt-get install` after its repo is set up. A name with other characters is refused when the agent starts. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_AGENTS` | none | The agents you chose in setup, comma-separated (`claude`, `codex`, `opencode`, `pi`, `free-pi`). `setup --check-only` reads it; when it is not set, claude is assumed. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_CHECK_SECONDS` | 60 | Setup only: how long to wait for the test request that checks your Claude token. |
| `CLOUDY_CLOUD_NO_ANIMATION` | unset | Setup only: set to `1` to skip the animated banner. The banner is also skipped when `CI` is set or there is no terminal. |
| `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT` | 1800000 | Claude Code's timeout for one MCP tool call, in milliseconds. The launcher sets it only if you have not. |
| `NO_COLOR`, `CLICOLOR=0`, `TERM=dumb` | unset | Any of these turns off colour and the animated setup display. Output is plain text with the same messages. |

> Note: You can set `CLOUDY_CLOUD_STARTS_PER_MIN`, `CLOUDY_CLOUD_MAX_INSTABOX_CALLS`, `CLOUDY_CLOUD_WORKER_HOURS`, `CLOUDY_CLOUD_TURN_MINUTES`, `CLOUDY_CLOUD_MAX_DEPTH`, `CLOUDY_CLOUD_MAX_AGENTS_PER_SESSION`, `CLOUDY_CLOUD_PROXY_SECRETS` and `CLOUDY_CLOUD_APT_PACKAGES` in the config file as well as in the environment.

### Files

| Path | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/env` | The config file. One `NAME=value` per line, mode 600. `cloudy-cloud setup` writes it. Only the settings and keys listed above are read from it, plus `CLOUDY_CLOUD_COORDINATOR_SNAPSHOT`, which `coordinator image --save` writes. Change the location with `CLOUDY_CLOUD_CONFIG`. |
| `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/codex-auth.json` | Optional. A copy of `~/.codex/auth.json` (mode 600) for the `codex-chatgpt` profile. Create it with `install -m 600 ~/.codex/auth.json ~/.config/cloudy-cloud/codex-auth.json`. Set `CLOUDY_CLOUD_CODEX_AUTH` to use another path. |
| `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/profiles.json` | Optional. Adds or overrides model profiles, including each profile's `harness`. See [Models and keys](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/models.html). |
| `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/mcp.json` | Optional. The MCP servers that cloud subagents get, in Claude Code's `mcpServers` format, mode 600. `cloudy-cloud mcp add` writes it. Secret values are stored as `${MCP_<NAME>_TOKEN}` references unless you used `--allow-literal`. See [MCP servers for subagents](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/mcp.html). |
| `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/events.jsonl` | The event log. The MCP server appends one JSON line per agent event (agent, message, machine, status, progress, reply). The file has mode 600 inside a folder with mode 700. It holds your prompts and replies, so it stays on your computer. Key-shaped text is redacted before writing, and each text is cut at 20,000 characters. It is never rotated: delete it to clear the history. The dashboard reads the newest 16 MB. |
| `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/owner` | An id the MCP server writes next to the config file, so `coordinator finish` can tell which running machines are its workers. You do not need to edit it. |

If you used the tool under its old name, claude-cloud, the first run copies `~/.config/claude-cloud` to `~/.config/cloudy-cloud` and renames the `CLAUDE_CLOUD_` keys in the config file. The old folder is left in place.


---

Source: https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/fleets.html

# Coordinators and fleets

> Run a cloud coordinator that manages many workers, and the limits that apply.

A coordinator is a Claude Code session that starts and manages many worker agents, each on its own cloud machine. This page covers when to use one, how to run one, and how to merge many worker branches into one pull request.

A coordinator always runs Claude Code, whichever agent is your main session, and it cannot use a pi, omp, Codex or opencode profile. Its workers can run any agent through `profile`. A coordinator needs a Claude login even when your main session is Codex, opencode, pi or free-pi: each coordinator signs in to Claude for itself when it starts (see below), and the coordinator's own session is Claude Code. Whether a coordinator can start `codex-chatgpt` workers has not been checked, and the code does not copy your ChatGPT login file (`codex-auth.json`) to a coordinator machine, so plan on `codex-chatgpt` not working from a coordinator.

**Worker credentials on a coordinator.** A coordinator can start a worker only if its machine holds that profile's key. On Instabox, `coordinator start` attaches every provider key that is stored as a proxy secret (listed in `CLOUDY_CLOUD_PROXY_SECRETS`), including `PARTICLE_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`, and the coordinator's `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/env` holds their names. So before you start a fleet that uses `codex` workers, store `OPENAI_API_KEY` as an Instabox secret and add it to `CLOUDY_CLOUD_PROXY_SECRETS` on your computer, as in [The codex profiles](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/models.html#codex-profiles). A key that is only a plain line in your env file is not sent; `coordinator start` says which keys it skipped. The opencode, pi and omp profiles use `PARTICLE_API_KEY` or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, which setup stores as proxy secrets.

### Picking a worker agent for a fleet

Keep the coordinator and any sub-coordinators on Claude Code. For the workers, set `profile` per task. For bulk, well-specified work (renames, adding tests, filling in similar files, doc updates), use an open-model profile: `glm`, `deepseek` or `particle` (Claude Code), `pi-glm` or `pi-deepseek`, or `omp-glm`. These are the ones verified live. Use `openrouter`, or `codex-openrouter` and `opencode-openrouter`, only with a `model` argument. Keep the default Claude profile for judgment-heavy tasks. Codex and opencode workers are not verified on a real machine (see [the status table](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/models.html#verified)), so try one before you start many. The `cloud-fleet` skill is a Claude Code skill.

## When to use a coordinator

For a few independent tasks, start plain cloud agents from your own session. You wait for them and review their branches yourself.

Use a **cloud coordinator** when all of these are true:

- The job is long or large.
- You want to leave, or close your laptop.
- The work needs only what is already on GitHub.

Do not hand a job to a cloud coordinator if it needs untracked local files, secrets or services that exist only on your laptop, or if you want to steer it step by step. Run the fleet from your own session instead.

There is also a lighter option. A cloud agent started with `role: "coordinator"` is a Claude subagent that can start its own cloud agents. Use this to build a tree: a coordinator, sub-coordinators for separate areas of the code, then workers. It lives only as long as your session. A cloud coordinator (below) runs on its own machine and keeps working with your laptop closed.

## Cloud coordinator lifecycle

### 1. Make the coordinator image (once)

Remote Control needs a full Claude login. A token from `claude setup-token` cannot open Remote Control sessions. Each coordinator signs in to Claude for itself when it starts, so the image carries no sign-in and a copied credential can never race several coordinators into signing each other out.

```
cloudy-cloud coordinator image
```

This creates a machine and installs `cloudy-cloud` on it. The command then removes `~/.claude/.credentials.json` on the image machine — so no Claude credential is ever frozen into a snapshot — saves the snapshot as `CLOUDY_CLOUD_COORDINATOR_SNAPSHOT` in `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/env`, and deletes the image machine.

The server deletes the image machine after 2 hours, and the command prints the time. If the machine is still running, `cloudy-cloud coordinator image --save` saves the snapshot the same way.

### 2. Start a coordinator

```
cloudy-cloud coordinator start NAME --repo https://github.com/OWNER/REPO --branch main --task-file brief.md
```

- `NAME`: lowercase letters, digits and `-`, up to 40 characters.
- `--repo`: a github.com https URL. The coordinator clones it into `~/repo`.
- `--branch B`: the branch to clone. Optional.
- `--task TEXT` or `--task-file PATH`: the brief. Optional, up to 100 KB. Without one, the coordinator waits for you.
- `--max-hours N`: when the server deletes the machine. Default and maximum 24.
- `--model NAME`: the Claude Code model for the coordinator's session, such as `opus` or `claude-opus-5-5`. Optional.
- `--json`: print the machine name, Remote Control name and attach command as JSON, with `started: true`.

The coordinator sees only the brief and the repo on GitHub. Commit and push everything it needs first. Give it exact acceptance commands, the files each work package owns, and a default for every question you can foresee, because nobody is there to answer.

A fresh coordinator then waits at `claude auth login` — a normal state the machine is never deleted for. On a terminal, `start` (and `cloudy-cloud cloud`) attaches you to the sign-in pane: open the URL it shows, sign in in your browser, and paste the code if asked. Off a terminal, `start` reports `needsLogin: true`, the `claude.ai` sign-in URL as `loginUrl` when the pane shows one, and `next: cloudy-cloud coordinator login NAME`. Finish the sign-in with `cloudy-cloud coordinator login NAME` (attaches to the pane on a terminal) or `cloudy-cloud coordinator login NAME --code CODE` (sends the code the browser showed; refused unless the pane is at the code prompt). `coordinator ls` and `coordinator status NAME` show `waiting for Claude sign-in` until then.

### 3. Reach it

- **Remote Control:** open claude.ai/code or the Claude app and pick the session named `NAME` (once the coordinator is signed in).
- **Terminal:** `cloudy-cloud coordinator attach NAME` opens its tmux session on a terminal. When piped, it prints that same command; run it in your own terminal.

The first time, attach once and accept any trust or Remote Control prompts. To list your coordinators, their delete times and any `waiting for Claude sign-in` state, run `cloudy-cloud coordinator ls`.

### 4. Finish or stop

- The coordinator ends its own job with `~/cloudy-cloud/bin/cloudy-cloud coordinator finish`. This deletes its machine only if the working tree is clean, the current branch and every `fleet/*` branch are pushed, and no worker is still running. If a check fails it tells you what to fix. `--force` skips the git and worker checks.
- You can delete it at any time with `cloudy-cloud coordinator stop NAME`.
- If neither happens, the server deletes the machine at its deadline.

> Warning: A coordinator is billed until it is stopped, finished or deleted. Its `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/env` holds the names of your proxy secrets, and its own Claude sign-in (`~/.claude/.credentials.json`, created when you finish `coordinator login`) is a real login. Anyone who can SSH into the machine can use them. Use an account you can revoke.

## Getting one result from many workers

Each worker pushes a branch named `cloudy-cloud/<id>`. Starting 100 workers is easy. Reviewing 100 pull requests is not. The `cloud-fleet` skill teaches Claude these patterns:

| Situation | Pattern |
|---|---|
| Many unrelated small fixes, and reviewers want separate PRs | Flat fan-out: one PR per branch. Keep it to about 10 to 15. |
| One feature or one large job split across many workers | Trunk merging (the default) |
| Stage B needs the merged result of stage A | Waves |
| More than about 50 workers, or clearly separate areas | Trunk merging with sub-coordinators |

### Trunk merging

The coordinator creates an integration branch `fleet/<topic>` and is the only one that merges into it.

Create and push the trunk before starting workers. Workers copy only tracked files, so commit everything they need first.

```
git fetch origin
git checkout -b fleet/<topic> origin/<base>
git push -u origin fleet/<topic>
```

2. Start the workers. Give each a brief with its goal, the files it owns, the base branch `fleet/<topic>`, the exact test command, and an instruction to push to its `cloudy-cloud/<id>` branch before it finishes.

As workers finish, fetch their branches and merge them one at a time, running the tests after each merge:

```
git fetch origin 'refs/heads/cloudy-cloud/*:refs/remotes/origin/cloudy-cloud/*'
git checkout fleet/<topic>
git merge --no-ff origin/cloudy-cloud/<id> -m "Merge <description> (<id>)"
git push origin fleet/<topic>
```

4. On a conflict, resolve small ones yourself, or abort the merge and ask the worker to rebase. If the tests fail after a merge, do not push it. Send the worker the failing output.
5. When every good branch is merged and the full tests pass, open one PR from `fleet/<topic>`.
6. Delete merged worker branches: `git push origin --delete cloudy-cloud/<id>`, or run `cloudy-cloud branches prune --yes` to delete every empty or merged `cloudy-cloud/<id>` branch (without `--yes` it only lists them). Keep the branch of a failed worker until you decide what to keep.

> Note: Do not trust a worker that says it is done. Fetch its branch, read the diff and run the tests before merging. If a worker pushed nothing, retry it with a narrower brief that names what is missing.

Only push to `cloudy-cloud/*` and `fleet/*` branches. Never push to `main`. Protect your main branch with a GitHub ruleset, because workers run with permission checks off.

### Sub-coordinators and waves

For large jobs, the top coordinator gives each area to a sub-coordinator with its own sub-trunk `fleet/<topic>/<area>`. Each sub-coordinator merges its workers, tests its area, and reports. The top coordinator merges the sub-trunks and opens the PR. Git cannot hold both `fleet/x` and `fleet/x/y`, so if that happens name them `fleet/<topic>-<area>`.

For waves, merge wave 1 into the trunk and push it before you start wave 2. Never start a dependent worker before its dependency is merged and pushed.

Keep coordinators on Claude Code, because merging and judging results needs a strong model. Open-model workers suit bulk, well-specified tasks. See [Models and keys](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/models.html). Check their branches more carefully.

## Limits and costs to watch

| Limit | Value |
|---|---|
| Cloud coordinator delete deadline | 24 hours by default and at most; set shorter with `--max-hours N`. It cannot be extended. A job that must run longer needs a new coordinator from a pushed branch. |
| Worker and nested coordinator delete deadline | `CLOUDY_CLOUD_WORKER_HOURS`, default 6, at most 24 |
| Idle agent | Stopped after 60 minutes with nothing to do |
| One task | Stopped after 29 minutes |
| Nesting depth | `CLOUDY_CLOUD_MAX_DEPTH`, default 3 |
| Agents per session | `CLOUDY_CLOUD_MAX_AGENTS_PER_SESSION`, default 200 |
| Start rate | `CLOUDY_CLOUD_STARTS_PER_MIN`, default 25 a minute. Extra agents show as `queued`. |
| Instabox calls at once | `CLOUDY_CLOUD_MAX_INSTABOX_CALLS`, default 24 |

Every machine in a tree counts against your Instabox machine limit and start rate. If many agents stay `queued`, the machine limit is full. Wait, or use fewer, larger tasks. Stop agents you no longer need with `cloud_agent_stop`, because idle agents cost money until they time out.

> Warning: Only work pushed to GitHub survives. A worker's unpushed work is lost with its machine. When you stop a coordinator, its workers are deleted by its cleanup process or at their own deadline (6 hours by default), so stop or collect them first. Machines your laptop session started are deleted when that session ends, so push or collect their work before you exit.

To see what is running, use the [dashboard](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/dashboard.html).


---

Source: https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/dashboard.html

# Dashboard and app previews

> Watch your cloud agents in a local web page and open apps running on their machines.

The dashboard is a read-only web page on your own computer that shows your cloud agents and the messages between them and your session. To look at an app a cloud agent is running, use `cloudy-cloud open`.

The dashboard and `cloudy-cloud open` work for every main session (Claude Code, Codex, opencode, pi, free-pi) and every worker agent (Claude Code, pi, oh-my-pi, Codex, opencode), because they read the event log that the cloud tools write. The Model column shows the profile name for a worker on another agent.

## Start the dashboard

```
cloudy-cloud dashboard
```

This prints a link and opens it in your browser. The page is served from `127.0.0.1` on port 4477, or on a free port if 4477 is taken. Press Ctrl+C in the terminal to stop it.

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--demo` | Shows sample data, so you can look around before you have started any agents. |
| `--port N` | Uses port N (0 to 65535). |
| `--no-open` | Prints the link without opening a browser. |

## What it shows

The page has two views, switched at the top: **List** and **Fleet**.

- **List** has the boxes in a left column and the selected box in a detail pane. Workers started by a cloud coordinator are nested under it; use the arrow next to the coordinator, or the Left and Right arrow keys, to close or open them.
- **Fleet** shows one tile per box, with its status, description, id and time since last activity, and a *Workers of* heading under each coordinator. Select a tile to open it in the List view.

In the Fleet view, boxes whose brief names a trunk branch (`fleet/<topic>`) get their own section above the groups. The section heading says how many of the workers' branches are merged into that trunk, and each tile says *merged* or *not merged*. The check runs `git branch -r --merged origin/<trunk>` in the folder where the dashboard runs, and is cached for about 30 seconds. If git cannot answer, the heading says *merge status unknown*. Other boxes are grouped as below.

Boxes are grouped as **Needs you**, **Active** and **Finished**.

- **Needs you:** agents that are idle, and agents that failed today.
- **Active:** agents that are queued, starting or running.
- **Finished:** everything else.

The top bar counts running, starting, idle and failed agents and those finished today. The browser tab title shows the failed and idle counts.

### The detail pane

Select a box to see:

- **Status**, **Model** (or profile), **Started**, **Role**, **Started by** (this session, or the coordinator that started it) and the **Machine**.
- **Harness**: the agent that runs the worker (`claude`, `pi`, `omp`, `codex` or `opencode`). It also shows as a tag on the box.
- **Autofix**: for an agent started with `autofix`, the state (for example running, with the round and the most rounds) and a link to the pull request, taken from the progress and result lines. It is shown only when the agent's text has them.
- **MCP**: the names of the MCP servers the subagent has, when it has any.
- **Branch**: the `cloudy-cloud/<id>` branch, with the result of the last push (the commit hash, or "push failed"), and copy buttons.
- **Deletes**: when the machine is expected to be deleted, for an agent that is still active or idle. For an idle agent this is 60 minutes after it went idle. For an active agent the dashboard shows the deadline recorded when the machine started; 6 hours after the start is only the fallback when the log has none. The server deletes a worker machine at its own deadline, 6 hours after it starts by default (`CLOUDY_CLOUD_WORKER_HOURS`, at most 24). On microsandbox the deadline only stops the microVM; a later cleanup removes it.
- **Open app**: for a running or idle agent, the command `cloudy-cloud open <id> <port>` with a copy button. See below.
- **Activity**: a timeline of the task you sent, follow-up messages, and the agent's replies, with what the agent did between them. Each step has a time. The agent's text is a block. Each tool call shows its name and its input as sent, cut at 4 KB, with a *Show all* button. Each tool result is one line, in green or red, that you can expand. Retries and errors are highlighted. A *Thinking* step shows only its length unless the dashboard runs with `CLOUDY_CLOUD_STREAM_THINKING=1` — the stored copy keeps the (redacted) raw stream lines either way, so the flag decides what the page shows, not what is saved. Each turn ends with a footer of tokens, cost and duration. When an agent has more than one turn, a *Turn* selector picks which one to read.
- **Source badge**: next to the timeline, it says where those steps came from and how old they are: *live from machine* with the seconds since the last read, *from local log* (a copy kept on this computer), *cached copy* (the machine is deleted), or *unavailable* with the reason.
- **Live tail**: while the selected agent is working, the page reads new steps every 2 seconds and shows *Working* with the time of the last step. It stops when you select another box or the tab is hidden. Other boxes are not read.
- **Terminal** (cloud coordinators only): a read-only copy of the coordinator's tmux session, refreshed every 3 seconds while the tab is open. To work in it, run `cloudy-cloud coordinator attach <name>`; the tab has a copy button for the command.

### When something is wrong

- **Offline:** the page cannot reach the dashboard server. It keeps the last list, shows the time of the last update, and retries every 3 seconds. If it has no list yet, it shows *The dashboard cannot reach its server*. Start the server again with `cloudy-cloud dashboard` and open the new link.
- **Old link:** each run makes a new link. A link from an earlier run is refused: a page that is already open shows *This link is from an earlier run*, and a request without the right token gets the text *This dashboard link is missing its access key, or it is from an earlier run.* Open the newest link in your terminal, or run `cloudy-cloud dashboard` again.
- **Live machines unavailable:** a banner appears if the Instabox machine list cannot be read, for example when `INSTABOX_API_KEY` is missing or invalid. Session history still shows.
- **No boxes yet:** an empty list means you have not started an agent from a `cloudy-cloud` session.

## What it cannot show

- **Sessions started before the event log existed.** Their agents have no history. If the machine is still running, it appears as a machine with no messages and a note that it has no title.
- **Machines started before stream capture existed, and machines deleted before any copy was kept.** The badge says *unavailable* and the timeline explains why, so it shows no tool calls. Only the messages in the session log appear.
- **A coordinator that is not running.** While a cloud coordinator's machine is running, the dashboard reads that machine's own event log and shows its workers with their prompts and replies, even for workers whose machines are already deleted (they appear as stopped, with the source "coordinator-log"). It reads at most one part of that log every 10 seconds, and only while the page is open. Once the coordinator's machine is deleted, nothing more can be read from it, and its workers appear only as far as their own machines or earlier cached copies show.
- **A cloud coordinator's own messages.** A cloud coordinator runs on its own machine, so its messages are not recorded on your computer. Its workers are listed under it, and the Terminal tab shows what is on its screen now, not its history. Nested coordinators log on their own machine too.
- **Queued agents.** A queued agent is shown as *starting*.
- **Ended sessions.** An agent from a session that has since ended is shown as stopped.

## Security model

- **Local only.** The server listens on `127.0.0.1`. It answers only requests whose `Host` is `localhost` or `127.0.0.1`.
- **Per-run token.** Each run makes a random token that is part of the link. A request without it gets a 401.
- **Read-only.** It accepts only GET and HEAD requests. It cannot start, message or stop an agent.
- **Keys stay out of the browser.** The Instabox key is used only by the server. Error text is redacted before it is sent to the page.
- **The event log is private to you.** The log is `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/events.jsonl` (set `CLOUDY_CLOUD_EVENTS` to move it), in a folder with mode 700, with file mode 600. Exact secret values are removed, and key-shaped text such as `sk-…`, `ghp_…`, `NAME_KEY=…` and bearer tokens is redacted, before anything is written. Each text is cut at 20,000 characters.

> Note: Prompts and replies can contain your code, and redaction only catches key-shaped text. Treat the log as private. It is never rotated; delete the file to clear the history. The dashboard reads the newest 16 MB of it.

## Reach an app running on an agent's machine

If an agent starts a dev server or a web app, you can view it from your own browser. The dashboard shows the command for each running agent in its **Open app** row. Replace `<port>` with the port the app uses.

### Private tunnel

```
cloudy-cloud open AGENT_ID 3000
```

This forwards `http://127.0.0.1:3000` on your computer to port 3000 on the agent's machine, until you press Ctrl-C. Use an agent id from `cloud_agent_list` (the `<id>` in branch `cloudy-cloud/<id>`), a machine name or a machine id. A coordinator's machine is named `coord-NAME`. To use a different local port, write `LOCAL:REMOTE`, for example `8080:3000`. Only you can reach the tunnel.

### Share a private link

```
cloudy-cloud open AGENT_ID 3000 --share
```

This prints a private link with a token in the URL. It never publishes the app publicly.

> Warning: Anyone who has the link can open the app, until the machine is deleted or you remove the link. Share it only with people who should see the app, and do not paste it where others can read it.

Remove the link with:

```
cloudy-cloud open AGENT_ID 3000 --unshare
```

`--share` and `--unshare` take a single port, not `LOCAL:REMOTE`.

### Two limits

**Start the app in the background.** A turn's foreground processes end with the turn. Ask the agent to run the app like this:

```
nohup npm run dev > /tmp/dev.log 2>&1 &
```

2. **The tunnel and link stop when the machine is deleted.** A worker machine is deleted after 60 idle minutes, when the session ends, or at its deadline (6 hours by default). A coordinator lives longer (24 hours by default).

The command uses the Instabox CLI (`npx --yes instabox@latest`), so you must be signed in to Instabox. If it says you are not, run `cloudy-cloud setup`. If the agent's machine is not running, the command says so and you need to start a new agent.

For running many agents, see [Coordinators and fleets](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/fleets.html).


---

Source: https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/mcp.html

# MCP servers for subagents

> Choose which of your MCP servers cloud subagents get with cloudy-cloud mcp add, what is allowed, and how tokens stay in Instabox.

Cloud subagents have no MCP servers unless you choose some. `cloudy-cloud mcp add` copies a server from your Claude Code settings to the list that every cloud subagent gets. It is off until you add one.

## Add a server

This page describes the Instabox provider, where the real token is stored as an Instabox secret. On other providers the token step differs and the command prints its own instruction: on self-hosted the value is delivered only under the `--allow-literal` consent path below, and on microsandbox named secret references are not supported, so a token reaches a worker only that same way.

Three steps. Replace `notion` with the name of the server in your Claude Code settings (`claude mcp list` shows it). `mcp add` reads only Claude Code's settings, whichever agent is your main session, so a server that is set up only in Codex, opencode or pi must be added to Claude Code first, or written into `mcp.json` by hand.

1. Copy the server: `cloudy-cloud mcp add notion`. It finds the server in your Claude Code settings, shows what it found, and saves it.
2. If the server needs a token, run the `secrets set` command that step 1 printed. You run it once per token.
3. Start subagents as usual. The reply ends with a line such as `MCP servers: notion`.

This is the output for a server that sends a token in a header:

```
cloudy-cloud mcp add notion
Found notion in ~/.claude.json (user scope):
  type     http
  url      https://mcp.notion.com/mcp
  headers  Authorization: Bearer ntn_…9f3a
This server sends a secret. Cloud machines run agents (Claude Code, pi, oh-my-pi, Codex and opencode alike) with permission checks off, so the value is not copied.
It is written as ${MCP_NOTION_TOKEN}; Instabox adds the real value to requests to mcp.notion.com only.
  Store it once:  printf %s "$TOKEN" | npx --yes instabox@latest secrets set MCP_NOTION_TOKEN --host mcp.notion.com
Added notion to ~/.config/cloudy-cloud/mcp.json. Every cloud subagent you start from now on gets it.
```

Run the stored-once command with the real token in `$TOKEN`. It must be an Instabox secret created with your `instabox login` session. Creating a secret with the Instabox API key from your cloudy-cloud config fails with `missing_scope: workspace:admin`. If you have not signed in, run `npx --yes instabox@latest login` first.

The list is read each time a subagent starts, so you do not need to restart `cloudy-cloud`. Subagents that are already running keep the servers they started with.

### Where the server is found

It searches your Claude Code settings in this order and uses the first match: the local scope (the entry for the current folder in `~/.claude.json`), the project scope (`.mcp.json` in the repo root), then the user scope (`mcpServers` in `~/.claude.json`). The first output line says which one it used. If the name is not found, it prints `No MCP server named NAME in your Claude Code config. See: claude mcp list` and exits with status 1.

If the name is already in the list, the command prints `Replacing the existing NAME entry.` and overwrites it.

This page applies to every worker agent: Claude Code, pi, oh-my-pi (`omp`), Codex and opencode. The list is the same for all of them. Only the file it is written to on the machine, and which servers are skipped, differ (see Files and what the machine gets). `cloudy-cloud mcp add` reads your Claude Code settings, so it works whichever agent you use as your main session, but the server must be in Claude Code's configuration. If you use Codex, opencode, pi or free-pi and have no Claude Code settings, there is nothing for `mcp add` to copy: install Claude Code, add the server there, then run `mcp add`, or write `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/mcp.json` by hand in the format below.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `cloudy-cloud mcp add NAME` | Copies one server from Claude Code's settings to `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/mcp.json`. A token is replaced by a reference and the command to store it is printed. |
| `cloudy-cloud mcp add NAME --allow-literal` | The consent path. See Putting the real token on the machine. |
| `cloudy-cloud mcp ls` | Lists the servers subagents get, one per line: name, type, target (the host, or the `npx` or `uvx` package) and the secrets it needs. With none, it prints `No MCP servers are shared with cloud subagents. Add one with: cloudy-cloud mcp add <name>`. |
| `cloudy-cloud mcp rm NAME` | Removes one server from the list. It does not delete the Instabox secret; use `npx --yes instabox@latest secrets rm MCP_NAME_TOKEN` for that. |

Any other `cloudy-cloud mcp` command, such as `cloudy-cloud mcp list`, goes to Claude Code's own `claude mcp`.

## What can be copied

A cloud machine cannot reach your computer, so only two kinds of server work:

- **Remote servers** of type `http` or `sse` with an `https` URL on a public host. Headers are allowed.
- **`npx` and `uvx` servers** (stdio). The command must be exactly `npx` or `uvx`, because those are installed on the machine.

Everything else is refused with a reason on the line `Not added: REASON`, and `mcp add` exits with status 1:

| Reason you may see | Why |
|---|---|
| `the command is X; only npx and uvx servers can run on a cloud machine` | A local program or script is not on the machine. |
| `arg X is a local path, which does not exist on the machine` | An argument starts with `/`, contains `~` or has a `..` part. |
| `url points at localhost, which does not exist on the machine` | The host is `localhost`, `*.local`, `0.0.0.0`, `::1`, or a `127.*`, `10.*`, `192.168.*` or `172.16-31.*` address. |
| `url must be https` | Plain `http` URLs are not copied. |
| `uses OAuth sign-in, which a headless subagent cannot complete` | A subagent cannot open a browser to sign in. |
| `uses headersHelper, a local script the machine does not have` | The script would not exist on the machine. |
| `type X is not supported on a cloud machine` | Only `http`, `sse` and stdio are accepted. |
| `url carries a secret value; send it in a header instead, ...` and `an argument carries a secret value; pass it in env instead, ...` | A key in a URL or an argument would sit on the machine as plain text. Instabox replaces tokens only in request headers. |
| `references ${X}; cloud machines only expand MCP_<NAME>_TOKEN secrets` | Other `${...}` variables are not available on the machine. |

The same checks run again every time a subagent starts, on whatever is in `mcp.json`.

> Warning: These are limits of the current version: no OAuth servers, no servers that run from a local path or listen on localhost, no secrets in URLs or arguments, no `sse` servers for the `pi` profiles (pi has no SSE transport), and no `sse` servers for the Codex profiles (Codex has none either). See the per-agent rules below.

## Tokens and secrets

Without `--allow-literal`, the token is never written to `mcp.json`. `mcp add` replaces each secret value in `env` or `headers` with `${MCP_<NAME>_TOKEN}`. `NAME` is the server name in capitals with `-` changed to `_`, so `notion` becomes `MCP_NOTION_TOKEN`. A second secret on the same server is `MCP_<NAME>_2_TOKEN`, and so on. A header is treated as secret when it is `Authorization`, its value starts with `Bearer`, its name ends in `KEY`, `TOKEN`, `SECRET` or `PASSWORD`, or the value looks like a known key format. The same name rule applies to `env` values.

You store the real value once in Instabox with the command `mcp add` prints:

```
printf %s "$TOKEN" | npx --yes instabox@latest secrets set MCP_NOTION_TOKEN --host mcp.notion.com
```

- For a remote server, `--host` is the URL's host.
- For an `npx` or `uvx` server, `mcp add` asks `Which HTTPS hosts does this server send the token to? (comma-separated, exact hostnames, required)`. It does not accept an empty answer. It also needs a terminal for that question. Without one it prints `Not added: a secret without a host list would be sent to any host the subagent reaches.`
- Never create the secret without `--host`. Instabox would then add the value to a request to any host, so a prompt injection could send it to a server the attacker controls.
- Instabox replaces the placeholder only in HTTPS request headers sent to the listed hosts. Both `Authorization: Bearer ...` and a custom header name were checked this way, from `curl` and from Node `fetch`. To other hosts the machine's placeholder stays a placeholder.

When a subagent starts, all the secret names it needs are attached to its machine together with `GH_TOKEN`. If one does not exist, the start fails with a message such as:

```
The Instabox secret MCP_NOTION_TOKEN could not be attached. Create it with: printf %s "$TOKEN" | npx --yes instabox@latest secrets set MCP_NOTION_TOKEN --host <host>
```

If the Instabox error does not name the secret, the message is the usual `GH_TOKEN` one, followed by `Secrets tried: GH_TOKEN, MCP_NOTION_TOKEN`.

Two server names that map to the same secret name (`my-srv` and `my_srv`) cannot both be added. `mcp add` prints `Not added: OTHER already uses MCP_MY_SRV_TOKEN. Rename one of the two servers in Claude Code first.`

> Note: A subagent can still *use* the token against the listed hosts, the way it can use `GH_TOKEN` against GitHub. It cannot read the real value.

### Putting the real token on the machine

Some servers cannot work with a placeholder, for example one that does not send the token in a header. For those, `cloudy-cloud mcp add NAME --allow-literal` keeps the real value in `mcp.json` and copies it to the machine of each subagent you start. A coordinator's own session gets it, but the workers a coordinator starts do not: consent is not passed down, so those workers skip the server. It only applies to values in `env` and `headers` that `mcp add` recognized as secret-looking. It is off unless you pass the flag.

> Warning: With `--allow-literal`, the real token is written into the worker's own config file with mode 600 — `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/mcp.json` for a Claude Code worker, `~/pi-agent/mcp.json` or `~/omp-agent/mcp.json`, `~/codex-home/config.toml` for a Codex worker, or `~/opencode-agent/opencode.json` for an opencode worker. Cloud machines run agents (Claude Code, pi, oh-my-pi, Codex and opencode alike) with permission checks off, so a prompt injection in a web page or file could make the agent send that token anywhere. Use a token you can revoke and that has the least access it needs.

The command prints this warning, then asks `Copy the real NAME token onto cloud machines? [y/N]`. Anything other than `y` or `yes` cancels it with `Not added. Run without --allow-literal to keep the token in Instabox.` It also needs a terminal, so you can confirm. Without one it prints `Not added: --allow-literal needs a terminal so you can confirm.` No Instabox secret is created for a server added this way. The entry in `mcp.json` gets `"cloudyCloudAllowLiteral": true`, which is removed before the file is sent to the machine. Remove the server with `cloudy-cloud mcp rm NAME`.

## Files and what the machine gets

- `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/mcp.json` on your computer, in Claude Code's own format: `{"mcpServers": {...}}`. `mcp add` writes it with mode 600 in a folder with mode 700. Set `CLOUDY_CLOUD_MCP` to use another path. If the file does not exist, the feature is off and nothing changes. If it is not valid JSON, `cloud_agent` fails with `Could not read FILE: ...` and the parse error.
- On each cloud machine, the checked servers are written to `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/mcp.json` (mode 600), and Claude is started with `--mcp-config` for that file and `--strict-mcp-config`. This is the Claude Code way of loading the file: it happens only for Claude Code workers and only when at least one server passed the checks. Workers on other agents get the same servers through their own config file, as the next items describe.
- On a Codex worker the servers go into `~/codex-home/config.toml`. Codex has no SSE transport and does not expand `${...}`, so it skips `sse` servers and entries that put a secret reference inside a longer value. A header must be exactly the secret or `Bearer ` plus the secret. The reply names each skipped server and the reason.
- On an opencode worker the servers go into `~/opencode-agent/opencode.json` (mode 600). opencode accepts `sse` servers. An entry whose value contains `{env:...}` or `{file:...}` is skipped, because opencode would replace it with a variable or file from the worker. Use a `${MCP_<NAME>_TOKEN}` reference instead (`mcp add` creates one).
- On a `pi` or `omp` worker the file goes to `~/pi-agent/mcp.json` or `~/omp-agent/mcp.json` instead (mode 600, folder mode 700). The servers and the `MCP_<NAME>_TOKEN` Instabox secrets are the same. `pi` has no SSE transport, so `sse` servers are skipped for `pi` workers and the reply says `MCP servers skipped: NAME (pi does not support the SSE transport)`. `omp` accepts `sse` servers, but skips an entry whose header or env value starts with `!` or is a bare variable name, because omp would run it or replace it with the worker's own variable. `omp` is also set to ignore MCP servers from other tools and from the repo's own config, so only these servers load.
- Because of `--strict-mcp-config`, a repo's own `.mcp.json` is not loaded on the machine once you have a server in the list. Without the list, nothing changes from before.
- Coordinators get the same list. The list holds references, not secret values, so it adds no secret to a coordinator machine.

## See which servers a subagent had

- **The reply footer** ends with a line such as `MCP servers: notion, context7 (failed: linear)`. It lists the servers that connected and, in brackets, the ones that did not. If none connected it says `MCP servers: none connected`.
- If you allowed a real token, another line says `MCP servers with a real token on the machine (you allowed it): NAME`.
- Entries that did not pass the checks appear as `MCP servers skipped: NAME (REASON)`.
- For a pi, omp, Codex or opencode worker the line is `MCP servers: a, b`, the names of the servers that were delivered to the machine. Unlike Claude's start-up report, it does not confirm that a server connected.
- **`cloud_agent_list`** shows a line `mcp notion, context7` under each subagent that has servers.
- **The dashboard** shows an MCP row in the agent's details with the server names. It never shows entries or tokens.

The footer lines appear only when the list has servers or skipped entries.


---

Source: https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/self-hosted.html

# Run on your own machine

> Run Cloudy Cloud subagents in Docker containers on a Mac or Linux computer you own, reached over SSH or Tailscale.

Instead of Instabox, subagents can run in Docker containers on a computer you own, such as a Mac Studio or a Linux server. Cloudy Cloud reaches it over SSH. Tools, branches and follow-ups work the same way.

This page applies to the main sessions and worker agents the same way as on Instabox, except for the key handling described under Keys for other agents. The provider itself is not yet verified live, and no Codex, opencode, pi or omp worker has been run on a self-hosted machine. Statuses for every agent: [what has been verified](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/models.html#verified).

## How it works

Set `CLOUDY_CLOUD_PROVIDER=self-hosted` (setup does this). Each subagent gets its own container on the machine, named `cc-<id>`, started from a worker image that setup builds there. Cloudy Cloud runs every command through one shared SSH connection and uses `docker exec` inside the container. The reaper that deletes a session's machines also removes that session's containers.

> Warning: On your own machine there is no proxy to hide the GitHub token. If you allow it, the token is stored inside each worker container for as long as it runs. See The GitHub token.

## What the machine needs

### A Mac

- **Remote Login.** Turn it on in System Settings, General, Sharing. This is the macOS SSH server.
- **An SSH key.** Remote Login with a key needs your public key in `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` on the Mac. Cloudy Cloud never asks for a password (it runs `ssh` with `BatchMode=yes`). Test with `ssh user@host true`.
- **Tailscale**, on the Mac and on your computer, so you can reach the Mac by its Tailscale name or `100.x` address from anywhere. Tailscale's own SSH server runs only on Linux, so on a Mac you use Remote Login with a key over the tailnet.
- **Docker Desktop or OrbStack.** Open it once so its engine is running. Setup looks for the `docker` program and saves its full path, because a non-interactive SSH session on a Mac does not have `/opt/homebrew/bin` on its `PATH`.
- **No sleep.** A sleeping Mac stops every subagent on it. In System Settings, Battery (or Energy), turn on "Prevent automatic sleeping when the display is off", or run `sudo pmset -a sleep 0` on the Mac. Doctor warns when the Mac is set to sleep.

### Linux

- Docker (or Podman) installed and running. Setup finds `docker` first and `podman` second.
- SSH access with a key, or Tailscale SSH (`sudo tailscale up --ssh`), in which case you need no key.

Either way, about 20 GB of free disk is expected for the worker image and containers. Setup and doctor warn below that.

## Run setup

```
cloudy-cloud setup --provider self-hosted
```

Without `--provider`, the installer asks "Where should subagents run?" and you type 2. Setup then asks, in order:

1. **SSH address** (`user@host`), for example `me@mac-studio`.
2. **Path to your SSH key**, optional. Press Enter to use your default keys or Tailscale SSH.
3. **How many subagents may run at once.** The suggestion is half the CPUs or one per 4 GB of memory, whichever is lower, and at least 1. On a Mac the container VM's own CPU and memory limit counts if it is lower than the Mac's.
4. **Allow the GitHub token on the machine?** Default is no. If you say yes, it asks you to paste a token. Nothing shows as you paste.

Between the questions it checks SSH, sleep (Mac), the container runtime and free disk, then builds the worker image `cloudy-cloud-worker:<version>` on the machine. The first build takes several minutes. It then saves the settings to `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/env` (mode 600). Run setup again after you update Cloudy Cloud, because the image version must match.

## The GitHub token

Subagents need a GitHub token to push their branches. On Instabox the token never reaches the machine. On your own machine it has to. If you answer yes at setup:

- The token is saved as `GH_TOKEN` in the config file, and `CLOUDY_CLOUD_SELF_HOSTED_TOKEN_ON_BOX=yes` records your consent.
- For each worker, the token is written over SSH standard input into a file on a memory-only filesystem inside the container (`/run/secrets/env`, mode 600). It is not in a command line, a container label or `docker inspect`, and it disappears with the container.
- Every `cloud_agent` reply says `GitHub token: on your machine <host> (you allowed it)`.

If you answer no, workers will not start, because they could not push. A subagent that runs on the machine can read the token while it runs, and it can push to any branch the token reaches. Use a fine-grained token limited to the repositories subagents may push to, and protect your main branch. Allow the token only on a machine you own and trust.

## Check the machine

```
cloudy-cloud doctor
```

Doctor checks the saved machine and prints one line per check, marked `ok`, `warn` or `fail`, with a `fix:` line under each problem. It exits with status 1 if any check fails. If the provider is not `self-hosted` it says so and checks nothing. It covers:

- SSH reachability and how long it took. A slow answer may mean Tailscale check mode is asking you to sign in again. Give the machine an "accept" rule or a longer `checkPeriod` in the Tailscale admin console, or use a normal key.
- Sleep settings, on a Mac.
- The container runtime, its path and version. A rootless Podman gets a warning that limits may not apply.
- Free disk, with a warning under 20 GB.
- The worker image, and whether its version matches Cloudy Cloud.
- Capacity: whether your slot count is above what the machine suggests.
- Running Cloudy Cloud containers, and a warning for any that is past its deadline, with the command to remove it.
- Saved settings: the container path, the slot count, and the GitHub token consent.

## Slots and sizing

The number of subagents at once is `CLOUDY_CLOUD_SELF_HOSTED_SLOTS`. Past it, a new subagent waits with the status `queued` and starts when one ends. Setup also saves a per-container limit that splits the machine between the slots: CPUs (`CLOUDY_CLOUD_SELF_HOSTED_CPUS`, at least 1) and 80% of memory (`CLOUDY_CLOUD_SELF_HOSTED_MEMORY`). On a Mac, "the machine" means the container VM's limits, which you set in Docker Desktop or OrbStack. If you raise them there, run setup again.

## Cleanup and deadlines

Each container runs `timeout <seconds> sleep infinity` as its main process and is started with `--rm`. It exits at its deadline (at most 24 hours) and Docker removes it, even if your computer is off. The client also deletes a session's containers when the session ends. To see and remove them yourself:

```
ssh user@host /path/to/docker ps -a --filter label=cloudy-cloud.purpose
ssh user@host /path/to/docker rm -f cc-<id>
```

Doctor prints these with your real values. What happens to containers when the machine reboots has not been checked yet. Doctor lists any that are left over.

## Previewing an app

`cloudy-cloud open <agent> <port>` works. It forwards a port on your computer to the container over SSH. `--share` does not work on this provider, because it cannot publish links.

## Limits

- **One machine.** Setup saves one SSH address.
- **Coordinators use Docker images.** `cloudy-cloud coordinator image --save` removes `~/.claude/.credentials.json` on the image container first — the image never holds a Claude sign-in, because each coordinator signs in for itself at `coordinator start`/`coordinator login` — then runs `docker commit --pause=true` and saves it as `cloudy-cloud-coordinator:<name>` on the machine. The image never holds `/run/secrets` (a tmpfs), so no token is saved either. `coordinator start` creates a container from it. You list and remove images with `docker image ls` and `docker rmi` on the machine; `cloudy-cloud` has no command for that. This has not been run live on a real Mac Studio yet.
- **Coordinators start workers through Docker.** Setup asks once: Coordinators on <host> can start containers through Docker, which gives them full control of Docker on that machine. Allow? If you say yes, a coordinator container gets the machine's Docker socket (workers never do) and starts its workers as sibling containers, so no SSH key is copied onto it. Its settings file holds the Claude credential and sizing settings, plus the GitHub token only if you allowed it, and never the SSH host or key; the coordinator's own Claude sign-in is created on the container when you finish `coordinator login`, never in the image. The risk: a coordinator can control every container on that machine. Without the consent, coordinators are refused and the reply says to run setup. Docker only, not Podman.
- **No published links.** `open --share` is refused.
- **Docker and rootless Podman.** Docker is the supported route. Podman is accepted but its limits may not apply when rootless.
- **Other agents in the worker image.** The worker image `cloudy-cloud-worker` contains Claude Code only (see `docker/worker.Dockerfile`). A worker on pi, omp, Codex or opencode installs its agent when it starts, from a pinned version with npm (omp with its own installer), so the container needs network access to the npm registry. No such worker has been run on a self-hosted machine. Main sessions (Codex, opencode, pi, free-pi) run on your computer and reach a self-hosted provider through the same `cloudy-cloud codex`, `opencode`, `pi` and `free-pi` commands; only the provider settings in the env file differ. free-pi cannot be a worker.
- **Keys for other agents.** A self-hosted machine has no proxy secrets, so a provider key such as `PARTICLE_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY` is a plain `NAME=value` line in `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/env`, and a worker that uses it holds the real value. The `codex-chatgpt` profile reads `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/codex-auth.json` as on Instabox.
- **Setup asks for no Instabox key.** It uses the saved agent list or the agents it finds on PATH, then asks for the keys they need: a Claude token only if you chose claude, an OpenAI key for codex workers (`--more` asks when codex is chosen or installed; plain setup only when no other worker credential is saved), and optional model provider keys. The Claude token is used only by Claude Code workers and coordinators (see [Getting started](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/index.html#agent-credentials)).
- **The agent can reach your network.** A container on your machine can reach the other devices that machine can reach.

## Docker Desktop: image build fails over SSH

Docker Desktop on a Mac can store registry logins in the macOS keychain (`credsStore` in `~/.docker/config.json`). A build started over SSH cannot unlock the keychain, so pulling the base image can fail with an error about credentials. The image uses `node:22-bookworm-slim`. Two ways around it:

- On the Mac itself, in a Terminal window, run `docker pull node:22-bookworm-slim`, then run setup again. The build then finds the base image locally.
- Use OrbStack instead.

This is a known Docker Desktop behavior. It has not yet been checked on the Mac Studio.


---

Source: https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/troubleshooting.html

# Troubleshooting, security and FAQ

> Fix common errors, see which credentials reach the cloud, and read answers to common questions.

Find the message you see, what causes it, and the command that fixes it. The security and FAQ sections follow.

## Troubleshooting

This page applies to every main session (Claude Code, Codex, opencode, pi, free-pi) and every worker agent (Claude Code, pi, oh-my-pi, Codex, opencode). Entries that apply to one agent say so.

### "cloudy-cloud is not set up yet"

A key is missing from `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/env`. In a terminal, `cloudy-cloud` asks `Run setup now? [Y/n]`. Without a terminal it exits with status 1. Run setup yourself:

```
cloudy-cloud setup
```

If you changed a key but the session still uses the old one, restart `cloudy-cloud`. Provider keys and `CLOUDY_CLOUD_PROXY_SECRETS` are re-read from the env file before each new subagent, but the Instabox key is read once, at start.

### The installer rejects a key

- `Got 103 of 108 characters, so it looks cut off`: the Claude token was cut short when pasted. Press Enter at the Claude step so the installer gets the token itself, or copy the whole token again.
- `Got N of 56 characters` or `starts like an Instabox key`: the Instabox key is incomplete or has a typo. The dashboard shows a key only once. If you lost it, create a new one at https://dashboard.instabox.sh/dashboard/api-keys.
- `Claude rejected this token`: the token is revoked or from another login. Run `cloudy-cloud setup` and press Enter at the Claude step.
- `Stopped the ... step after 3 tries`: nothing was changed and the saved key stays. Run `cloudy-cloud setup` again.

### "malformed API key" or 401 from Instabox

The Instabox key is wrong or revoked. Run `cloudy-cloud setup`, replace the key, and restart `cloudy-cloud`.

### `npm install -g cloudycloud` fails with EEXIST

The package was renamed from `cloudy-cloud` to `cloudycloud`. The old package can leave a `cloudy-cloud` link in npm's global `bin` folder that points nowhere, and npm refuses to install over it. The error names the file, for example `EEXIST: file already exists, symlink ... /bin/cloudy-cloud`. Remove that file, then install again:

```
rm <the path shown in the error>
npm install -g cloudycloud
```

`cloudy-cloud setup` finds this link and offers to remove it for you.

### No git repository, or no github.com origin

The launcher warns `This folder is not a git repository, so subagents can't start here.` or `This repo has no github.com origin, so subagents can't push their work.` Run `cloudy-cloud` from inside a repo and add an origin:

```
git remote add origin https://github.com/OWNER/REPO.git
```

Your GitHub token must also include that repository.

### A turn failed or hit the time limit

Each turn is limited to 29 minutes by default (`CLOUDY_CLOUD_TURN_MINUTES`, a whole number from 5). If a turn fails or hits the limit after the agent has started, the agent stays `idle` with its session and the machine. The result is marked as an error. Send `cloud_agent_message` with a message such as "continue where you stopped". A Codex or opencode first turn that times out still fails, because those agents do not report their session id early.

### The GitHub access check failed, or "Push failed"

`The GitHub access check for origin cloudy-cloud/<id> failed` (the setup check runs `git ls-remote origin HEAD`) usually means the `GH_TOKEN` Instabox secret is missing or the token cannot write to this repo. Run `cloudy-cloud setup`, replace the GitHub token, and check the token's repository list. The secret must be named exactly `GH_TOKEN`. The same fix applies to `The GH_TOKEN Instabox secret could not be attached`.

If the worker committed nothing, no branch is pushed and the result says `No changes, no branch pushed.` That is not a failure.

After each task, `cloudy-cloud` pushes once more, retrying once after five seconds. If that fails, the result says `Push failed: ...; the agent is still open, ask it to push.` It may also list `Uncommitted changes left in the sandbox`. The tool never commits for the agent. While the agent is open, ask it to commit and push.

### "The sandbox could not be reached to push"

The machine is gone or not answering. The result continues: `Only work the agent already pushed to origin cloudy-cloud/<id> survives.` Fetch that branch:

```
git fetch origin cloudy-cloud/<id>
```

Unpushed work on that machine is lost. A failed agent cannot take messages. Use `cloud_agent_wait` to read the error, then `cloud_agent_stop`.

### "Subagent failed, exit code N"

The agent run on the machine exited with an error. The paragraph below is for Claude Code workers; for Codex see Codex problems for opencode, pi and omp see opencode, pi and oh-my-pi problems.

For a Claude Code worker, the run exited with an error. The result includes its error output, the push status and the token totals. If the output says `Not logged in · Please run /login` or shows a 401, no valid Claude token reached the machine. Run `claude setup-token`, then `cloudy-cloud setup` and replace the Claude token, then restart. This also happens if you only export `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, because wrappers such as cmux's `claude` remove it.

### The agent for `cloudy-cloud codex`, `opencode`, `pi` or `free-pi` is not found

- Codex: `the codex command was not found.` Run `npm install -g @openai/codex`.
- opencode: `opencode is not installed.` Run `npm install -g opencode-ai`.
- pi and free-pi: if `pi` or `free-pi-cli` is not on your PATH, Cloudy Cloud runs a pinned copy through `npx`, so Node.js and network access are needed. If registering the tools fails it prints `Could not register the cloud tools with free-pi` with the command to retry.
- All four need the Instabox key (or the self-hosted settings). Without it they print `cloudy-cloud is not set up yet` and tell you to run `cloudy-cloud setup`.

### "Profile NAME needs KEY, which is not set"

The profile's provider key is missing: `PARTICLE_API_KEY` for the pi, omp and opencode profiles, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` for the OpenRouter profiles, `OPENAI_API_KEY` for `codex`. Add it with `cloudy-cloud setup` (Particle.ai and OpenRouter) or as described in [The codex profiles](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/models.html#codex-profiles) (OpenAI). If the message says the key is set as a real value, not as a proxy secret, store it as an Instabox secret: on Instabox a real key is never copied to a machine.

### Codex problems

- `The Codex ChatGPT login file ... was not found`: sign in on your computer with `codex login` (choose "Sign in with ChatGPT"), then run `install -m 600 ~/.codex/auth.json ~/.config/cloudy-cloud/codex-auth.json`.
- `The Codex login file ... can be read by other users`: run `chmod 600 ~/.config/cloudy-cloud/codex-auth.json`.
- A 401 or an expired token with `codex-chatgpt`: run `codex login` again and repeat the `install` command above.
- `model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account`: start the worker without `model`, or use a model your plan supports.
- `incorrect api key` with `codex`: check `OPENAI_API_KEY` in your Instabox secrets and in `CLOUDY_CLOUD_PROXY_SECRETS`.
