Codex and opencode workers are not verified on a real machine ([status table](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/models.html#verified)). If one fails in a way not listed here, the error text in the result is the best clue; please report it.

### A subagent stays "queued"

Starts are paced (`CLOUDY_CLOUD_STARTS_PER_MIN`, default 25 a minute), or your Instabox plan's machine limit is full (`quota_exceeded`). Paused machines count toward the limit. A subagent blocked by the quota retries every 60 seconds for up to 30 minutes, then fails with Instabox's message. Stop subagents you do not need, delete leftover machines (below), or upgrade the plan.

If you see `rate_limited` after 5 tries, lower `CLOUDY_CLOUD_STARTS_PER_MIN` and restart `cloudy-cloud`.

### An agent was stopped for being idle

An agent with nothing to do is stopped after 60 minutes and its machine is deleted. A message to it then returns `Agent <id> is not open. It may have been stopped, been idle for 60 minutes, or never existed.` A single task is also stopped after 29 minutes. Start a new subagent from the branch the old one pushed.

### "This session has already started N agents"

One session may start 200 agents by default. Stop idle agents or raise `CLOUDY_CLOUD_MAX_AGENTS_PER_SESSION`.

### Leftover machines

When a session ends, a separate cleanup process deletes that session's machines, even after a hard kill. It deletes only machines labelled with that session's id, so it never touches coordinators. Instabox also deletes every machine at its delete deadline (6 hours by default for workers, 24 at most). To check by hand:

```
npx instabox@latest ls
npx instabox@latest rm <name>
```

Machines made by this tool have the label `purpose=cloudy-cloud`. To stop a cloud coordinator, run `cloudy-cloud coordinator stop NAME`.

### What is on the cloud machine

Machines start from Instabox's `agent-browser` image. cloudy-cloud does not build it. Present: Chromium at `/usr/bin/chromium`, Docker, Node, pnpm, git and gh. Absent: `ffmpeg`, `psql` and `agent-browser`. The disk is 20 GB, with about 16 GB free after the image.

- **Extra packages.** Set `CLOUDY_CLOUD_APT_PACKAGES="ffmpeg postgresql-client"` in `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/env`. Each new worker then runs one `sudo -n apt-get install` for those names after the repo is set up. Names must match `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.+-]*`, or the agent is refused at start. With the setting empty, nothing extra runs.
- **Chromium with Playwright.** Launch it with `executablePath: "/usr/bin/chromium"` and the argument `--no-sandbox`.
- **Playwright in a pnpm monorepo.** `playwright` may not resolve from the repo root, because pnpm does not hoist it. Import the copy under `node_modules/.pnpm/playwright-core@*/node_modules/playwright-core` instead.

### The session says the built-in Agent tool is unavailable

This is expected. `cloudy-cloud` turns off Claude Code's built-in `Agent` and `Workflow` tools. Ask for "a subagent" and it uses `cloud_agent`. Plain `claude` keeps its built-in tools.

### Dashboard problems

- `This dashboard link is missing its access key, or it is from an earlier run.` (a plain 401 page), or the heading `This link is from an earlier run` on an open dashboard page: you opened an old or edited link, or the dashboard was restarted. Open the newest link that `cloudy-cloud dashboard` printed, or run it again. The token changes on every run.
- `The dashboard cannot reach its server`, or the banner `The dashboard server is not answering` (the list may be out of date): the dashboard process stopped. Run `cloudy-cloud dashboard` again and open the new link.
- `Live machines unavailable.`: the page could not list machines from Instabox. Check your connection and that `INSTABOX_API_KEY` in `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/env` is still valid. Session history still shows.

See [Dashboard and app previews](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/dashboard.html) for the full dashboard guide.

### MCP server problems

- `The Instabox secret MCP_..._TOKEN could not be attached`: the secret does not exist. Create it with `printf %s "$TOKEN" | npx --yes instabox@latest secrets set MCP_NAME_TOKEN --host HOST`. Creating a secret needs your `instabox login` session, not the API key.
- `MCP servers skipped: NAME (REASON)` at the end of a reply: the entry in `mcp.json` did not pass the checks for that worker's agent. Fix the entry (in Claude Code's settings, then `cloudy-cloud mcp add NAME` again) and see [MCP servers](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/mcp.html#files) for each agent's rules: Codex skips `sse` servers and entries that put a secret reference inside a longer value; opencode skips entries that contain `{env:...}` or `{file:...}`; pi skips `sse` servers; omp skips values that start with `!` or are a bare variable name.
- `MCP servers: ... (failed: NAME)`: the server was sent but did not connect on the machine. Check the token, the host in `--host` and the server's address.
- `Could not read FILE: ...`: `mcp.json` is not valid JSON. Fix or delete the file.

See [MCP servers for subagents](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/mcp.html) for what a cloud machine can and cannot run.

## Security

### opencode, pi and oh-my-pi problems

- `Could not install opencode in the sandbox`, `Could not install pi in the sandbox` or `Could not install omp in the sandbox`: the worker installs its agent when it starts, so the machine needs network access to npm (omp: `omp.sh`). The message ends with the install error.
- opencode, a provider key is missing: opencode reads its key name from `~/opencode-agent/opencode.json` on the worker. The profile needs `PARTICLE_API_KEY` (`opencode-glm`, `opencode-deepseek`, `opencode-particle`) or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (`opencode-openrouter`, which also needs `model`). See Profile NAME needs KEY.
- A follow-up to an opencode, pi, omp or Codex worker fails, or the result says `No valid session_id came back, so the agent cannot be resumed`: a first turn that failed has no session to continue. Start a new agent instead of sending a message.
- pi and omp workers: read the error text in the result. If the `MCP servers skipped` line names a server, see [MCP servers](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/mcp.html#files) for why.
- `free-pi` stops at its first-run consent prompt: `free-pi-cli` asks for consent the first time it runs, and that needs an interactive terminal. Start it once yourself in a terminal, answer the prompt, then use `cloudy-cloud free-pi`.

### What runs where

Your main session (Claude Code, Codex, opencode, pi or free-pi) and the `cloudy-cloud` tool server run on your machine. Each subagent runs its agent (`claude -p` by default, or pi, omp, Codex or opencode for a profile) on its own Instabox machine, on a snapshot of your repo's tracked files. Subagents run with permission checks off, so protect your main branch with a GitHub ruleset that blocks direct pushes. The GitHub token can push to any branch it reaches.

### Which credentials reach the cloud machine

- **Claude token:** placed on each Claude Code worker without a profile (and sent to cloud coordinators for their workers, where the launcher keeps it out of the coordinator's own session). It can only make model requests. Workers on pi, omp, Codex or opencode do not get it.
- **Coordinator sign-in:** a cloud coordinator's own Claude login (`~/.claude/.credentials.json`) is created on its machine when you finish `cloudy-cloud coordinator login NAME`. The coordinator image never holds it — the credential file is removed before the image is saved. It is a real login; use an account you can revoke.
- **GitHub token:** never reaches the machine. Instabox stores it as the secret `GH_TOKEN`. The machine sees a placeholder that Instabox's proxy replaces on requests to `github.com` and `api.github.com`.
- **Instabox key:** stays in `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/env` (readable only by you) and in the tool server. It is never put in process arguments.
- **MCP server tokens:** only for servers you added with `cloudy-cloud mcp add`. The token stays in Instabox as `MCP_<NAME>_TOKEN`, and the machine sees a placeholder that Instabox replaces in request headers to the host you named. The subagent can use the token against that host but cannot read it. Never create the secret without `--host`. With `--allow-literal` the real token is on the machine. See [MCP servers for subagents](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/mcp.html).
- **ChatGPT login file** (`codex-chatgpt` only): your `codex-auth.json` is written to the worker machine, even on Instabox, because it cannot be a proxy secret. Its tokens are scrubbed from replies. Revoke it by signing out in your ChatGPT account.
- **Provider keys** (for example Particle, OpenRouter, OpenAI): setup stores Particle.ai and OpenRouter keys as Instabox proxy secrets, so workers see a placeholder. A key you chose to keep in the env file sits on the worker machines that use it. See [Models and keys](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/models.html).

Create the GitHub token as a fine-grained token, limited to the repos you use, with Contents read and write, Pull requests read and write, Workflows read and write (to push files under `.github/workflows`), and Actions and Commit statuses read (so subagents and Autofix can see CI results).

### The dashboard is local only

The dashboard is a read-only page on `127.0.0.1`. Requests without the random per-run token, or with another `Host` header, are refused. Keys never reach the browser.

### The event log

The tool server appends one JSON line per event to `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/events.jsonl` (folder mode 700, file mode 600). Prompts can contain code, so the file stays on your machine. Exact secret values are scrubbed and key-shaped text is redacted before writing. The file is never rotated. Delete it to clear history.

### Revoking keys

Revoke the Instabox key in the Instabox dashboard, the GitHub token at https://github.com/settings/personal-access-tokens, the Claude token by revoking it in your Claude account, and any OpenAI, Particle.ai or OpenRouter key in that provider's dashboard. If you used `codex-chatgpt`, sign out in your ChatGPT account and delete the copy `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/codex-auth.json`, because that file is sent to worker machines. Then run `cloudy-cloud setup` to enter new ones. To remove saved keys from your machine:

```
rm ~/.config/cloudy-cloud/env
```

> Warning: On a cloud coordinator, `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/env` holds the real Instabox key, the Claude token and your provider keys, and `~/.claude/.credentials.json` holds its own Claude sign-in. Anyone who can SSH into the coordinator can read them. Use keys and an account you can revoke.

## FAQ

### What does it cost?

The tool itself has no price in this repo. You pay for your Instabox plan, your Claude subscription or API usage, and any open-model provider you use. The free Instabox plan is too small for more than a few subagents at once. Results end with a token total, and a cost when Claude reports one.

### Which models can subagents use?

Claude Code by default. A `profile` can run a worker on pi, oh-my-pi, Codex or opencode instead, with open models such as GLM and DeepSeek through Particle.ai, any model on OpenRouter, or OpenAI models through Codex. See [Models and keys](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/models.html).

### Does it copy untracked files?

No. A subagent gets files tracked by git, including uncommitted edits to them. Add a new file with `git add` if the subagent needs it.

### Can work continue with my laptop closed?

Not from a laptop session: subagents stop when the session ends. For work that must continue with the laptop closed, use a [cloud coordinator](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/fleets.html).

### What is kept after a subagent stops?

Only work pushed to GitHub on branch `cloudy-cloud/<id>`. The machine is deleted.

### Does it change plain `claude`?

No. Only sessions you start with `cloudy-cloud` use the cloud.

### How do I uninstall it?

Delete leftover machines first (see above). If you installed with `npx cloudycloud setup`, run:

```
npm uninstall -g cloudycloud
rm -rf ~/.config/cloudy-cloud ~/.claude/skills/cloud-fleet ~/.claude/skills/cloudy-cloud-setup ~/.claude/skills/cloud-dev
```

Remove a skill folder only if setup installed it (a copy it made); keep one you made yourself.

If you installed from a git clone, run `npm unlink -g cloudycloud` instead (also `npm unlink -g cloudy-cloud` for a clone from before the package was renamed), then delete the clone.

To delete only the empty or merged subagent branches on GitHub, run `cloudy-cloud branches prune` in your repo (a dry run), then `cloudy-cloud branches prune --yes`. To delete all of them, run this in your repo:

```
git ls-remote --heads origin 'cloudy-cloud/*' | awk '{print $2}' | xargs -n 50 git push origin --delete
```

### Is it affiliated with Anthropic?

No.


---

Source: https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/what-is-cloudy-cloud.html

# What is Cloudy Cloud?

> What Cloudy Cloud is, how it differs from running subagents locally, who it is for and what it costs.

Cloudy Cloud is open-source software (MIT license, install with npx cloudycloud setup) that gives every subagent of your coding agent its own cloud machine, a copy of your repo, and its own branch.

It works with Claude Code, Codex, opencode, pi and free-pi as your main session, and Claude Code, pi, oh-my-pi, Codex and opencode as the agent that runs on each cloud machine. Claude Code is the default for both. free-pi can only be a main session.

## What is Cloudy Cloud?

Cloudy Cloud is a command, `cloudy-cloud`, that starts a coding agent (Claude Code by default) with an extra MCP server. The server adds tools such as `cloud_agent`. When your session hands work to a subagent, Cloudy Cloud creates a cloud machine, uploads a snapshot of your repo, runs the worker agent there (Claude Code by default), and pushes the result to a branch named `cloudy-cloud/<id>` on your GitHub repo.

In a `cloudy-cloud` session, the built-in `Agent` and `Workflow` tools are turned off, so subagents run in the cloud and not on your laptop. Sessions you start with plain `claude` are not changed. See [How it works](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/how-it-works.html) for each step.

## How is it different from running subagents locally?

Subagents that run on your laptop share its CPU, memory and battery with you, so their builds and tests can slow your session down. With Cloudy Cloud you still start and steer everything from your laptop, but each subagent runs on its own machine in the cloud.

- **Where it runs:** on a cloud machine, one per subagent.
- **What it sees:** files tracked by git in your repo, including uncommitted edits. It cannot see untracked files or your personal Claude settings. It has your MCP servers only if you copy them with `cloudy-cloud mcp add`.
- **What you get back:** a git branch per subagent, `cloudy-cloud/<id>`, pushed to your GitHub repo, plus a reply with the branch, commit and token totals.
- **How long it lives:** a subagent stops after 60 idle minutes or when your session ends. Its machine is deleted at a fixed deadline, 6 hours by default and 24 at most. Only work pushed to GitHub is kept.

## Who is it for?

It is for people who use a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, opencode, pi or free-pi) and want subagents to run on cloud machines instead of on their own computer. You need a GitHub repo you can push to, because each subagent pushes its work there.

For a long job that must keep going with your laptop closed, use a [cloud coordinator](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/fleets.html), which runs on its own machine.

## What do I need?

- An account with a cloud sandbox provider. Instabox is supported today.
- A credential for each kind of worker you run. For Claude Code workers and coordinators, a Claude subscription or API key. Workers on pi, oh-my-pi, Codex or opencode use another credential instead; see [Models and keys](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/models.html). Setup asks for a Claude token only if you use Claude; see [Getting started](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/index.html#agent-credentials).
- A GitHub repo you can push to.
- Node.js 20 or later.

Subagents run Claude Code by default. A profile can run them on open models such as GLM and DeepSeek, or on another agent: pi, oh-my-pi, Codex or opencode. See [Models and keys](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/models.html).

## What does it cost?

Cloudy Cloud is open source under the MIT license, and the tool itself has no price in this repo. You pay your own providers: your Instabox plan, your Claude subscription or API usage, and any other provider (OpenAI, open-model hosts) you use. The free Instabox plan is too small for more than a few subagents at once.

## How do I start it?

In a terminal, inside a git repo with a GitHub remote, run the command for your agent where you would run that agent: `cloudy-cloud` for Claude Code, `cloudy-cloud codex`, `cloudy-cloud opencode`, `cloudy-cloud pi` or `cloudy-cloud free-pi`. It opens a normal session of that agent; when the session uses a subagent, that subagent runs on its own cloud machine and pushes its work to the branch `cloudy-cloud/<id>`. `cloudycloud` is the same command, and `npx cloudycloud` works without a global install.

## How do I install it?

Run this once in a terminal:

```
npx -y cloudycloud setup
```

It checks your tools, offers to install the `cloudy-cloud` command, and asks for your keys. The steps are in [Getting started](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/). The source is on [GitHub](https://github.com/dennisonbertram/cloudycloud) and the package is [cloudycloud on npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/cloudycloud).

## Where to read next

- [FAQ](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/faq.html) for short answers.
- [Glossary](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/glossary.html) for the terms used in these docs.
- [Command and tool reference](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/reference.html) for every command and option.


---

Source: https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/faq.html

# FAQ

> Short answers about what Cloudy Cloud does, what it needs, what it keeps and how to remove it.

Short answers about what Cloudy Cloud does, what it needs, what it keeps and how to remove it.

## Questions

### What is a subagent?

When your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, opencode, pi or free-pi) hands a piece of work to a helper agent, that helper is a subagent. Cloudy Cloud runs each helper on its own cloud machine instead of on your laptop.

### How do I start Cloudy Cloud?

Run `cloudy-cloud` instead of `claude`, from inside a git repo with a GitHub remote. It starts a normal Claude Code session in which every subagent runs on its own cloud machine. To use another main session, run `cloudy-cloud codex`, `cloudy-cloud opencode`, `cloudy-cloud pi` or `cloudy-cloud free-pi`. `cloudycloud` is the same command; if you skipped the global install, use `npx cloudycloud`. Set it up first with `npx -y cloudycloud setup`.

### What do I need?

An account with a cloud sandbox provider (Instabox is supported today), a GitHub repo you can push to, Node.js 20 or later, and a credential for each agent your workers use: a Claude subscription or API key for Claude Code workers (the default), or the provider key for a profile (Particle.ai, OpenRouter or OpenAI, or a ChatGPT login for Codex). See [Models and keys](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/models.html).

### What can a subagent see?

Files tracked by git in your repo, including uncommitted edits. It can't see untracked files or your personal agent settings (for example your Claude settings). It has MCP servers only if you copy them with `cloudy-cloud mcp add`. Add a new file with `git add` if the subagent needs it.

### Can subagents use my MCP servers?

Yes, the ones you choose. Run `cloudy-cloud mcp add NAME` for each server. Remote `https` servers on public hosts and `npx` or `uvx` servers work. OAuth sign-in, localhost, local paths and secrets in URLs or arguments do not, and `pi` workers skip `sse` servers. Tokens stay in Instabox. See [MCP servers for subagents](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/mcp.html).

### What happens to the machines?

A subagent stops after 60 idle minutes or when your session ends. Its machine is deleted after 6 hours by default, 24 at most. Only work pushed to GitHub is kept.

### What is kept after a subagent stops?

Only work pushed to GitHub on branch `cloudy-cloud/<id>`. The machine is deleted.

### Is it safe?

Your GitHub token never reaches the cloud machine. Subagents run with permission checks off, so protect your main branch. The [setup guide](https://github.com/dennisonbertram/cloudycloud/blob/HEAD/docs/RUNBOOK.md) shows how. See [Security](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/troubleshooting.html#security) for which credentials reach the cloud machine.

### Does it change plain `claude`?

No. Only sessions you start with `cloudy-cloud` use the cloud.

### What does it cost?

The tool itself has no price in this repo. You pay for your Instabox plan, your Claude subscription or API usage, and any open-model provider you use. The free Instabox plan is too small for more than a few subagents at once. Results end with a token total, and a cost when Claude reports one.

### Which models and agents can subagents use?

Claude Code by default. A `profile` can run a worker on pi, oh-my-pi, Codex or opencode instead, with open models such as GLM and DeepSeek through Particle.ai, any model on OpenRouter, or OpenAI models through Codex. Status of each agent: [what has been verified](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/models.html#verified). See [Models and keys](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/models.html).

### Can I use my own computer?

Yes. Run `cloudy-cloud setup --provider self-hosted` to send subagents to a Mac or Linux machine you own, reached over SSH (for example through Tailscale). Each subagent runs in its own Docker container there. You must allow the GitHub token on that machine. Coordinators work through Docker images but have not been run live yet. See [Run on your own machine](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/self-hosted.html).

### Can work continue with my laptop closed?

Not from a laptop session: subagents stop when the session ends. For work that must continue with the laptop closed, use a [cloud coordinator](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/fleets.html).

### How do I uninstall it?

Delete leftover machines first. If you installed with `npx cloudycloud setup`, run `npm uninstall -g cloudycloud`, then delete `~/.config/cloudy-cloud`, `~/.claude/skills/cloud-fleet`, `~/.claude/skills/cloudy-cloud-setup` and `~/.claude/skills/cloud-dev` (only those setup installed; keep any skill folder you made yourself). The full steps, including the install-from-clone case and deleting the subagent branches on GitHub, are in [Troubleshooting](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/troubleshooting.html#faq-uninstall).

### Is there a hosted version?

Not yet. A hosted version is coming. Today Cloudy Cloud is open source (MIT) and you bring your own keys: your cloud account, your Claude credentials and your GitHub token.

### Is it affiliated with Anthropic?

No.

## More help

For error messages and fixes, see [Troubleshooting, security and FAQ](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/troubleshooting.html). For the terms used here, see the [Glossary](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/glossary.html).

# Glossary

> The terms used in the Cloudy Cloud docs, such as subagent, worker, coordinator, profile and delete deadline.

The terms used in the Cloudy Cloud docs, with one short definition each.

## Terms

### Subagent

A helper agent that your main session (Claude Code, Codex, opencode, pi or free-pi) hands a piece of work to. Cloudy Cloud runs each subagent on its own cloud machine instead of on your laptop.

### Cloud agent

A subagent started with the `cloud_agent` tool. It runs Claude Code by default, or pi, oh-my-pi, Codex or opencode when a profile says so. It runs in a remote sandbox on the committed and tracked files of your repo and pushes its work to its own branch.

### Worker

The default role of a cloud agent: it does the task it was given and does not start agents of its own.

### Coordinator

A cloud agent started with `role: "coordinator"`, which gets `cloudy-cloud` installed and can start its own cloud agents, limited by `CLOUDY_CLOUD_MAX_DEPTH` (default 3). A cloud coordinator is the longer-lived kind that runs on its own machine and keeps working with your laptop closed.

### Box (machine)

The cloud machine, an Instabox sandbox, that Cloudy Cloud creates for one cloud agent. It is deleted when the agent stops or at its delete deadline.

### Profile

A named setting that runs a worker on another model or another agent, such as `glm`, `pi-glm`, `omp-glm`, `codex`, `opencode-glm` or `openrouter`. With no profile, a subagent runs Claude Code. See [Models and keys](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/models.html).

### Harness

The coding agent that runs on a worker machine: `claude` (Claude Code), `pi`, `omp` (oh-my-pi), `codex` or `opencode`. A profile sets it, and `"harness"` sets it in `profiles.json`.

### Main session (host)

The coding agent you talk to, started with `cloudy-cloud` (Claude Code), `cloudy-cloud codex`, `cloudy-cloud opencode`, `cloudy-cloud pi` or `cloudy-cloud free-pi`. It gets the `cloud_agent` tools. It is separate from the harness of the workers it starts.

### MCP sync

The opt-in copy of chosen MCP servers from your Claude Code settings to cloud subagents, whichever agent each one runs (Claude Code, pi, oh-my-pi, Codex or opencode). You add each server with `cloudy-cloud mcp add NAME`. The list is saved in `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/mcp.json`, and tokens stay in Instabox. See [MCP servers for subagents](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/mcp.html).

### Branch cloudy-cloud/<id>

The git branch a subagent works on and pushes to your `origin` remote; `<id>` is the agent id shown by `cloud_agent_list`.

### Task mode

The way `cloud_agent` runs as a background task when your Claude Code supports MCP tasks, so its progress shows in `/tasks` and its result arrives on its own.

### Idle stop

Cloudy Cloud stops a subagent that has been idle for 60 minutes, and stops every subagent when the session ends.

### Delete deadline

The fixed time at which Instabox deletes a machine in any state: 6 hours by default for workers (set `CLOUDY_CLOUD_WORKER_HOURS`, up to 24) and at most 24 hours for a cloud coordinator. It cannot be extended, so push your work before it.

### Reaper

A separate cleanup process that the session starts. After the session is gone, even after a hard kill, it deletes every machine the session created.

### Setup-token

The long-lived token that `claude setup-token` creates (it starts with `sk-ant-oat01-`). It lets cloud agents use your Claude subscription, as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`.

### Event log

The file `~/.config/cloudy-cloud/events.jsonl`, where the MCP server appends one JSON line per agent event. It stays on your computer and the dashboard reads it.

### Dashboard

A read-only web page on your own machine, opened with `cloudy-cloud dashboard`, that shows every box and the messages between your session and each subagent.

## Related pages

See [How it works](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/how-it-works.html), [Command and tool reference](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/reference.html) and the [FAQ](https://cloudycloud.tech/docs/faq.html).
